title: Worked: equating real and imaginary parts

board_content.text: Two real equations from one complex equation.

segments_english.text: Here is Method B in action — turning one complex equation into two real ones and solving.
We're told, for real x and y, that four x plus i times three x minus y equals three plus i times minus six.
Match the real parts on both sides. On the left the real part is four x; on the right it is three. So four x equals three.
Now match the imaginary parts. On the left the imaginary part is three x minus y; on the right it is minus six. So three x minus y equals minus six.
From the first equation, x is three over four.
Substitute into the second: y equals three x plus six, which is nine over four plus six, giving thirty three over four.
Notice what happened: one complex equation split cleanly into two real equations, and each unknown fell out.
So the answer is x equals three over four and y equals thirty three over four.

segments_hinglish.text: Ye raha Method B action mein — ek complex equation ko do real equations mein badalna aur solve karna.
Humein bola gaya, real x aur y ke liye, ki four x plus i times three x minus y equals three plus i times minus six.
Dono taraf ke real parts match karo. Left par real part hai four x; right par three. To four x equals three.
Ab imaginary parts match karo. Left par imaginary part hai three x minus y; right par minus six. To three x minus y equals minus six.
Pehli equation se, x hai three over four.
Doosri mein substitute karo: y equals three x plus six, jo hai nine over four plus six, matlab thirty three over four.
Dekho kya hua: ek complex equation saaf do real equations mein bat gayi, aur har unknown nikal aaya.
To answer hai x equals three over four aur y equals thirty three over four.
